But when riches were there to monopolize, strongmen and inequalities emergedTVBy Tim Vernimmen11:00 AM CDT on September 7, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThis story was originally published by Knowable Magazine.Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 Introducing This Jellyfish-Inspired Robot That’s Going to Help Clean WaterwaysShareNextStayWhy are some societies ruled by autocrats — powerful people who make all the decisions with barely, if any, checks and balances — while in others, the governed actually have a say?If you ask an archaeologist, historian or political scientist, this is how the story traditionally goes: People used to move around in small groups to hunt and gather, making decisions more or less collectively. Then they invented agriculture, which tied them to particular patches of land, and allowed some of them to store and hoard resources. This inevitably led to inequality in wealth and power.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
